newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak FinMin says t-bill bid rates too high.
newsitem.headline: Slovak FinMin says t-bill bid rates too high.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry said it rejected all bids in its three-week treasury bill auction on Wednesday due to "unacceptably high" bids.
"The banks have simply gone too far ," Marian Horvath, head of the ministry's State Assets and Liabilities Department, told Reuters.
"We thought we would accept bids at between 13-15 percent, but demanding 15.3 to 22 percent for such short paper is unacceptable," Horvath said.
The ministry rejected all bids in an auction of its three-week t-bills, the first paper with such a maturity this year. Bids in auction totalled 1.28 billion crowns.
Average yield in the last successful auction of similar bills on November 28 was at 10.414 percent.
When asked whether the ministry would now consider direct foreign participation in t-bill auctions, Horvath said: "We are not ready yet for such a move."
Last January, the ministry said it may allow foreign investors access to treasury bill auctions to help refinance the state budget deficit.

The high bank bids in Wednesday's auction resulted from a shortage of liquidity on the domestic interbank money market which began at the beginnig of the year after central bank moves to reduce consumption-led credit expansion at commercial banks.
Rates on the interbank market on Wednesday ranged between 25 percent for o/n funds and 19.70 percent for six-month money.
The 1997 budget plans a 36.9 billion crown deficit, up from a 25.5 billion crown shortfall in 1996.
The 1997 state budget stipulates that the finance ministry is to issue a total 70 billion crowns in state securities this year to finance last year's and this year's deficits.
